text: Tax controller: homes 7 -> 4 (demand 0), shops 7 -> 4 (demand 0), factories 7 -> 3 (demand 0)
Claudeville 4 day one: a20-day1 (dense homes + parks, factories, shops, coal, 12 pumps, road + rail links). Audit passed.
Claudeville 4 attempt 1 started: goal 200,000 by 2050. Opening = the Claudeville 3 winner's day one; plan is to cross the river ~20 years sooner and fill the whole map, then arcologies after 120,000.
Late loan #2 (Jul 2002 vs Feb 2001 in attempt 19): 3,430 people vs 5,780 at the same date. Added a 500-person reminder for loan #2 to the pace file.
Jul 2002: loan #2 -> blocks 3-4 (a20-2003, $9,932); loan #3 -> coal plant (68,48) + 19 north pumps ahead of the shortage that hit attempt 19 here.

Aug 2004 loans #4-5: district 5 ($6,318), north district + coal (a19-2004, $6,403), zoo (110,56) ($3,002; a calibration test road left at (112,59) blocked it first - autocal now checks its test roads are gone). Finance ordinances + City Beautification (new ordinances.sh).
Tax controller: shops 8 -> 9 (demand 1958), factories 7 -> 8 (demand 2000)

Control failure: autocal's 6-tile edge margin (added in Claudeville 3) rejected almost every calibration spot near the east edge, so the east-homes build crawled, timed out twice and placed five 2x2 road patches where parks belonged (~$3,000 lost). Margin now 2 tiles (+4 south for the zoom check); roads cleared and parks placed in minutes.
Dec 2005: 14,160 people. The container restarted (save intact); then my own edge guard broke calibration near the map edge and cost ~$3,000. Fixed; resuming.

Dec 2006: river crossed 21 years earlier than Claudeville 3 - causeway ($275) on y69, raised wires on y68, first west district x20-40 y48-68 ($6,088), powered via a new line x59 y65-67. build.py's automatic bridge choice had a %-format bug (fixed; causeway picked by hand once).
Dec 2006: 18,630 people. Stadium, airport and the river crossing all done this year - the west half of the map is open 21 years earlier than last challenge.
Tax controller: homes 6 -> 7 (demand 1273)
Dec 2007 loan #10: second west district + marina + 11 pumps ($7,663), factory strip x17-19 ($1,198). Strip power routed around a park via x21 to a built home (audit caught it).
Tax controller: homes 7 -> 8 (demand 1206)
Tax controller: homes 8 -> 9 (demand 1040)
Oct 2008 loans #11-12: coal (68,52), second seaport, far-west strip x10-15 + coal (30,15), west shop band, factory pipe ($15,879 in all). Audit clean.
Oct 2008: 31,340 people - about 5,000 ahead of the Claudeville 3 winner at the same date. 12 loans.
Jul 2009: 36,140 people; east district 2 (homes around the pond + dense factories, $2,520) - attempt 19's plan with its fixes folded in.
Tax controller: homes 9 -> 8 (demand -375)
Feb 2010 loan #13: south district ($3,308) and south2 with zoo #2 ($6,301). Their lines leaned on districts not yet built in this attempt; audit caught it; joined to powered lines ($124).
Jul 2010 loan #14: ~30 pumps (lake + riverbanks, 94 in all) after spare water hit 1%; south-west block with stadium #2 ($8,283). Audit clean.
Jul 2010: 41,300 people - ~12,000 ahead of the Claudeville 3 winner. 14 loans; water crisis fixed; second stadium built.
Dec 2010 loan #15: south factory strip ($1,237), factory row y70-72 ($580), north-west district with a coal plant ($7,638). Audit clean.
Apr 2011: the stadium beside the airport burned down (16 rubble tiles). Loan #16: rubble cleared, stadium rebuilt, fire station (17,66) on the west bank ($5,565). No reload - rebuilt.
Apr 2011: 45,530 people. A fire destroyed the first stadium; rebuilt it and added a fire station. 16 loans.
Loan #17 to pay for a second, wider firebreak against the airport crash fire

The April 2011 plane crash fire is the worst disaster yet: it has burned most of the east bank, including the north district. Two-tile firebreaks were jumped, so I'm clearing a four-tile break to save the power plants and the seaport. The west bank is safe across the river.
Loans #18 and #19 to rebuild the east bank's roads, power lines and plants after the plane-crash fire

The fire is out (May 2011) but it destroyed almost the whole east bank: about 4,000 tiles of rubble, its roads and power lines gone. The zoning survived, and roads can be built straight onto rubble, so I'm rebuilding the east side's network from the original plans with two new loans. The west bank is untouched.

CONTROL failure: the east-bank rebuild ran out of cash (rebuilt plants took most of it) and build.py kept clicking with $0 for about an hour. build.py now stops with OUT OF CASH every 10 steps and before each gap round. Loan #20 taken; rebuilding the remaining roads and lines.

Feb 2012: bond payments $11k/yr vs taxes $2.6k/yr after the fire halved the city. Loan #21 only to pipe water to the dry far-west strip; home tax ceiling raised to 12%, factories to 10% (demand is maxed); no other spending until income recovers.

Zoo (117,98) and stadium (110,42) on burned land to lift the home cap at ~45,000; loans #22-23. CONTROL fix: build.py now clears rubble under plants, stations and recreation before placing them (the stadium failed on rubble).

Feb 2014: the city has bounced back from the fire to 44,030 people, back on the pace line. The catch is money: 23 loans cost about $12k a year and taxes bring in about $5.5k, so I only spend where it adds people. Just built a zoo and a stadium so homes can keep growing past 45,000.

Feb 2016: joined pipe networks that never linked (far-west strip, south-east corner; ~540 dry buildings). Loans #24-25 (cash was -$12k).
Tax controller: shops 6 -> 5 (demand -973), factories 7 -> 6 (demand -969)
Tax controller: factories 6 -> 5 (demand -779)

Feb 2018: 55,860 people and on pace. The city ran out of empty zoned land, so I'm building a new 12-block district on the empty south part of the west bank. Money is the weak spot: 27 loans now, and taxes cover only about half the yearly loan payments, so every loan has to add people.
Jul 2018: coal plant (117,84) fed into the x116 line - the far south-east was browning out (loan #28).
Tax controller: homes 9 -> 10 (demand 1159)
Tax controller: homes 10 -> 11 (demand 1081)

Dec 2020: 68,020 people, ahead of the pace line (62,750). Land ran out again and many west-bank homes were short of water, so I'm adding a pump row on the river and 18 more blocks south of the new district. 31 loans now; the bet is that each one adds enough people to be worth its yearly cost.
Tax controller: factories 5 -> 6 (demand 1029)

Dec 2021: zoo (50,98), stadium (50,111) and coal plant (50,106) east of district 3 (loans #32-33). CONTROL fix: the stadium dialog blocked the screen when Football was already taken; build.py now tries each team until Done shows.
Tax controller: homes 11 -> 10 (demand -382)
Feb 2023: 14 more riverbank pumps on the west shore (x58-59 y93-105) piped into the y94 and y108 rows - the west bank's pipes were watered only near their source (loans #34-35).

Feb-Apr 2023: a second plane crash at the airport set off another great fire that burned the east bank again (77,850 -> 48,240 people). Two lessons: the airport regrows on its zone and keeps crashing planes, so I removed it; and 3 fire stations for 78,000 people was far too few, so the rebuild adds 25 stations on a grid. Loans #36-39 pay for it.
